honorific: Forms of address and self-reference register sheet (zh→en): render royal and imperial first-person pronouns (孤, 朕, 寡人) as natural English 'I' (or majestic 'we' where fitting), never literally as 'lone' or 'the lone one'. Render courtier self-reference 臣 before a sovereign as 'Your servant' or 'Your subject' (preserving humble court register, never dropping it to bare 'I'), and render sovereign honorifics like 陛下/萬歲 as 'Your Majesty' (never literally 'Ten Thousand Years'). Render noble, official, clerical and humble self-references (本王, 下官, 妾身, 贫僧/貧僧, 弟子, 小人, 草民) naturally by speaker role and register ('I', 'this prince', 'this official', 'this humble woman', 'this poor monk'), avoiding awkward repetition (e.g. never 'this disciple took on a disciple'); capitalize recurring self-epithets consistently ('Old Sun', 'Old Pig', never lowercase 'old Sun'). Grade forms of address (大人, 殿下, 太公/員外, 公子, 先生, 师父/師父, 长老/長老) by speaker-to-listener rank ('Your Excellency', 'my lord', 'Old Master/Squire [Surname]', 'Your Highness', 'Master', 'Elder') rather than flattening distinct social ranks. Avoid stiff Chinese calques: drop demonstrative 'That' before a named character (那<Name> -> '<Name>'), and do not pluralize collective 師徒們 into 'disciples' when only one disciple is present. Preserve classical logic faithfully: keep negation scope across multi-clause imperatives (e.g. 莫…只管… means 'do not … and keep …', not an affirmative command), preserve correlative conditionals (不A，就B = 'if not A, then B'), keep exact arithmetic/share divisions, approximate numeric ranges (e.g. 三五 = 'three to five', 五七 = 'five or seven', never multiplication), traditional time units (一個時辰 = two hours; 不一日 = 'before many days', not 'less than a day'), agent/plaintiff-defendant direction (答应替他 = promised to do it for him), and kinship/generational seniority (distinguishing spouse's siblings from maternal aunts/uncles), and resolve classical idioms and allusions rather than translating their surface words literally.
